The level of transparency for scrollbars when a GUI is not running and `termguicolors` is not
set.

Must be between `0` (opaque) and `100` (transparent).

This option is ignored for scrollview windows whose highlight group has `reverse` or `inverse`
specified as a cterm attribute; see `|attr-list|`.
Such windows will have no transparency, as a workaround for Neovim #24159.

This option is ignored for scrollview windows shown for floating windows; see
`|scrollview_floating_windows|`.
Such windows will have no transparency, as a workaround for Neovim #14624.

options.description:

you often edit files on remote filesystems.

It's called unsafe because it improves the time `:Startify` needs to execute by reducing the
amount of syscalls to the underlying operating system, but sacrifices the precision of shown
entries.

This could lead to inconsistencies in the shown `:Startify` entries (e.g. the same file could be
shown twice, because one time file was opened via absolute path and another time via symlink).

options.description:
A list of Vim regular expressions that is used to filter recently used files.
See `|pattern.txt|` for what patterns can be used.

The following patterns are filtered by default:
- `'runtime/doc/.*\.txt$'`
- `'bundle/.*/doc/.*\.txt$'`
- `'plugged/.*/doc/.*\.txt$'`
- `'/.git/'`
- `'fugitiveblame$'`
- `escape(fnamemodify(resolve($VIMRUNTIME), ':p'), '\') .'doc/.*\.txt$'`

NOTE: Due to the nature of patterns, you can't just use "~/mysecret" but have to use
"$HOME .'/mysecret.txt'".
The former would do something entirely different: `|/\~|`.

NOTE: When using backslashes as path separators, escape them. Otherwise using
"C:\this\vim\path\is\problematic" would not match what you would expect, since `|/\v|` is a
pattern, too.

Example:
```nix
[
  "\.vimgolf"
  "^/tmp"
  "/project/.*/documentation"
]
```

options.description:
The configuration options for **tmux-navigator** without the `tmux_navigator_` prefix.

For example, the following settings are equivialent to these `:setglobal` commands:
- `foo_bar = 1` -> `:setglobal tmux_navigator_foo_bar=1`
- `hello = "world"` -> `:setglobal tmux_navigator_hello="world"`
- `some_toggle = true` -> `:setglobal tmux_navigator_some_toggle`
- `other_toggle = false` -> `:setglobal notmux_navigator_other_toggle`
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of lua value
options.title: plugins.tmux-navigator.settings

options.description:
By default, if you zoom the tmux pane running vim and then attempt to navigate "past" the edge of the vim session, tmux will unzoom the pane.
This is the default tmux behavior, but may be confusing if you've become accustomed to navigation "wrapping" around the sides due to this plugin.

This option disables the unzooming behavior, keeping all navigation within vim until the tmux pane is explicitly unzoomed.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.tmux-navigator.settings.disable_when_zoomed

options.description:
By default `<C-h>`, `<C-j>`, `<C-k>`, `<C-l>`, & `<C-\\>`
are mapped to navigating left, down, up, right, & previous, respectively.

This option disables those default mappings being created.

You can use `plugins.tmux-navigator.keymaps` to define your own custom mappings.
You will also need to **update your tmux bindings** separately,
if you want them to match.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.tmux-navigator.settings.no_mappings

options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.tmux-navigator.settings.no_wrap

options.description:
As noted in `disable_when_zoomed`, navigating from a vim pane to another tmux pane normally causes the window to be unzoomed.
Some users may prefer the behavior of tmux's `-Z` option to `select-pane`, which keeps the window zoomed if it was zoomed.

This option enables that behavior.

Naturally, if `disable_when_zoomed` is enabled, this option will have no effect.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.tmux-navigator.settings.preserve_zoom

options.description:
You can configure the plugin to write the current buffer, or all buffers, when navigating from vim to tmux.

null: don't save on switch (default value)
1: `:update` (write the current buffer, but only if changed)
2: `:wall` (write all buffers)
options.title: plugins.tmux-navigator.settings.save_on_switch

options.type: open submodule of attribute set of lua value
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings

options.description:
When disabled (default), giving an invalid count to the `|[%|` and `|]%|` motions and the text
objects `|i%|` and `|a%|` will cause the motion or operation to fail.

When enabled, they will move as far as possible.

Note: targeting high counts when this option is enabled can become slow because many positions
need to be tried before giving up.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.delim_count_fail

options.description:
If set to `1`, middle words (like `return`) are not matched to start and end words for
highlighting and motions.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.delim_nomids

options.description:
This option controls whether matching is done within strings and comments.

- By default, it is set to `0` which means all valid matches are made within strings and
  comments.
- If set to `1`, symbols like `()` will still be matched but words like `for` and `end` will
  not.
- If set to `2`, nothing will be matched within strings and comments.
options.type: null or one of 0, 1, 2 or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.delim_noskips

options.description:
When enabled (the default), the plugin will be loaded for all buffers, including ones without
a file type set.

This allows matching to be done in new buffers and plain text files but adds a small start-up
cost to vim.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.delim_start_plaintext

options.description:
Configures the number of lines to search in either direction while using motions and text
objects.
Does not apply to match highlighting (see `matchparen_stopline` instead).
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.delim_stopline

options.description: Set to `0` to disable the plugin entirely.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.enabled

options.description: Set to `0` to disable all mappings.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.mappings_enabled

options.description:
Deferred highlighting improves cursor movement performance (for example, when using `|hjkl|`)
by delaying highlighting for a short time and waiting to see if the cursor continues moving.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_deferred

options.description:
When set to `{time}` in milliseconds, the deferred highlighting behavior is changed in two
ways:

1. Highlighting of matches is preserved for at least `{time}` even when the cursor is moved
  away.
2. If the cursor stays on the same match for longer than `{time}`, highlighting is cleared.

The effect is that highlighting occurs momentarily and then disappears, regardless of where
the cursor is.
It is possible that fading takes longer than `{time}`, if vim is busy doing other things.

This value should be greater than the deferred show delay.
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_deferred_fade_time

options.description:
If the cursor has not stopped moving, assume highlight is stale after this many milliseconds.

Stale highlights are hidden.
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_deferred_hide_delay

options.description:
Delay, in milliseconds, between when the cursor moves and when we start checking if the cursor
is on a match.

Applies to both making highlights and clearing them for deferred highlighting.
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_deferred_show_delay

options.description:
This option can disable match highlighting at `|startup|`.

Note: vim's built-in plugin `|pi_paren|` plugin is also disabled.
The variable `g:loaded_matchparen` has no effect on match-up.

You can also enable and disable highlighting for specific buffers using the variable
`|b:matchup_matchparen_enabled|`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_enabled

options.description:
Configure the virtual symbol shown for closeless matches in languages like C++ and python.

```cpp
if (true)
  cout << "";
else
  cout << ""; ◀ if
```
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_end_sign

options.description:
Highlight buffer background between matches.
This uses the `MatchBackground` highlighting group and is linked to `ColorColumn` by default.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_hi_background

options.description:
Always highlight the surrounding words, if possible.
This is like `|<plug>(matchup-hi-surround)|` but is updated each time the cursor moves.

This requires deferred matching (`matchparen_deferred = 1`).
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_hi_surround_always

options.description: Adjust the timeouts in milliseconds for highlighting.
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_insert_timeout

options.description:
When not empty, match highlighting will be disabled in the specified modes, where each mode
is a single character like in the `|mode()|` function.

E.g., to disable highlighting in insert mode,
```nix
matchparen_nomode = "i";
```
and in visual modes,
```nix
matchparen_nomode = "vV\<c-v>";
```

Note: In visual modes, this takes effect only after moving the cursor.
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_nomode

options.description:
Attrs controlling the behavior with off-screen matches.
If empty, this feature is disabled.
options.type: null or (open submodule of attribute set of anything)

options.description:
For floating window on neovim only: set to add a border.
If the value is the integer `1`, default borders are enabled.

A list or string can be specified as described in `|nvim_open_win()|`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or list of string
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.border

options.description: For `"popup"` method: make the floating window as wide as the current window.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.fullwidth

options.description:
For popup method on vim only: set to a highlight group to override the colors in the
popup window.
The default is to use `*hl-Pmenu*`.
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.highlight

options.description:
Sets the method to use to show off-screen matches.
Possible values are:

- `"status"` (default): Replace the |status-line| for off-screen matches.\
  If a match is off of the screen, the line belonging to that match will be displayed
  syntax-highlighted in the status line along with the line number (if line numbers
  are enabled).
  If the match is above the screen border, an additional `Δ` symbol will be shown to
  indicate that the matching line is really above the cursor line.
- `"status_manual"`: Compute the string which would be displayed in the status-line or
  popup, but do not display it.
  The function `MatchupStatusOffscreen()` can be used to get the text.
- `"popup"`: Use a floating window to show the off-screen match.
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.method

options.description:
When enabled, off-screen matches will not be shown in the statusline while the cursor is
at the screen edge (respects the value of `'scrolloff'`).

This is intended to prevent flickering while scrolling with `j` and `k`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.scrolloff

options.description:
For popup method on vim only: syntax highlight the code in the popup.

options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_offscreen.syntax_hl

options.description: Whether or not to highlight recognized words even if there is no match.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_singleton

options.description:
The number of lines to search in either direction while highlighting matches.

options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_stopline

options.description: Adjust the timeouts in milliseconds for highlighting.
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.matchparen_timeout

options.description:
If enabled, cursor will land on the end of mid and close words while moving downwards
(`|%|/|]%|`).
While moving upwards (`|g%|`, `|[%|`) the cursor will land on the beginning.
Set to `0` to disable.

Note: this has no effect on operators: `d%` will delete `|inclusive|` of the ending word (this
is compatible with matchit).
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.motion_cursor_end

options.description: Set to `0` to disable motions (`|matchup-%|`, `|%|`, `|[%|`, `|]%|`).
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.motion_enabled

options.description:
In vim, `{count}%` goes to the `{count}` percentage in the file (see `|N%|`).
match-up overrides this motion for small `{count}` (by default, anything less than 7).

- For example, to allow `{count}%` for `{count}` less than 12, set it to `11`.
- To disable this feature, and restore vim's default `{count}%`, set it to `0`.
- To always enable this feature, use any value greater than 99.
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.motion_override_Npercent

options.description: Set to `0` to disable selecting matches with double click.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vim-matchup.settings.mouse_enabled

options.description:

To enable match-up for tex files, set this option to `1`.
This will replace vimtex's built-in highlighting and `%` map.

Note: matching may be computationally intensive for complex LaTeX documents.
If you experience slowdowns, consider also setting `matchparen_deferred` to `1`.

You may use `"v"`, `"V"`, and `"\<c-v>"` (i.e., an actual CTRL-V character) to specify the

options.description:

options.description:
Set this option to `1` to tell vimux to close the runner when you quit vim.

Caution: It is probably best not to mix this with `RunnerName`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.CloseOnExit

options.description:
- Set this option to `1` to enable shell completion in `PromptCommand`.
- Set this option to `0` to enable vim command editing in `PromptCommand`.

Enabling shell completion blocks the ability to use up-arrow to cycle through previously-run
commands in `PromptCommand`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.CommandShell

options.description:
If you're having trouble with vimux, set this option to get vimux to pass each tmux command to
`|echomsg|` before running it.
options.type: null or boolean or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.Debug

options.description:
Should the command given at the prompt via `PromptCommand` be expanded using `expand()`.

Set to `1` to expand the string.

Unfortunately `expand()` only expands `%` (etc.) if the string starts with that character.
So the command is split at spaces and then rejoined after expansion.
With this simple approach things like `"%:h/test.xml"` are not possible.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.ExpandCommand

options.description:
The part of the screen the split pane Vimux will spawn should take up.
This option accepts both a number of lines/columns or a percentage.
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.Height

options.description:
Allows additional arguments to be passed to the tmux command that opens the runner.

Make sure that the arguments specified are valid depending on whether you're using panes or
windows, and your version of tmux.
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.OpenExtraArgs

options.description:
The default orientation of the split tmux pane.

This tells tmux to make the pane either vertically or horizontally, which is backward from
how Vim handles creating splits.
options.type: null or one of "v", "h" or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.Orientation

options.description:
The string presented in the vim command line when Vimux is invoked.

Be sure to put a space at the end of the string to allow for distinction between the prompt
and your input.
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.PromptString

options.description:
The keys sent to the runner pane before running a command.

When vimux runs a tmux command, it first makes sure that the runner is not in copy mode by
running `copy-mode -q` on the runner.
This sequence is then sent to make sure that the runner is ready to receive input.

The default sends `C-u` to clear the line.
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.ResetSequence

options.description:
Setting the name for the runner.

Works for panes and windows.
This makes the VimuxRunner reusable between sessions.
Caveat is, all your instances (in the same session/window) use the same window.

Caution: It is probably best not to mix this with `CloseOnExit`.
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.RunnerName

options.description:
Set this option to define a query to use for looking up an existing runner pane or window
when initiating Vimux.

Uses the tmux syntax for the target-pane and target-window command arguments.
(See the man page for tmux).

It must be an attrs containing up to two keys, `pane` and `window`, defining the query to
use for the respective runner types.

If no key exists for the current runner type, the search for an existing runner falls back
to the `UseNearest` option (and the related `RunnerName`).

If that option is false or either command fails, a new runner is created instead, positioned
according to `Orientation`.
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.RunnerQuery

options.description:
The type of view object Vimux should use for the runner.

For reference, a tmux session is a group of windows, and a window is a layout of panes.
options.type: null or one of "pane", "window" or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.RunnerType

options.description:
The command that Vimux runs when it calls out to tmux.

It may be useful to redefine this if you're using something like tmate.
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.TmuxCommand

options.description: Use existing pane or window (not used by vim) if found instead of running `split-window`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.vimux.settings.UseNearest

Can be switched inside VM.
Leave empty to use your current setting.
options.type: null or one of "", "smart", "sensitive", "ignore" or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.case_setting

options.description:

It can be useful if you use keyboard layouts other than QWERTY.

Valid motions that you can remap are:
```
h j k l w W b B e E ge gE , ; $ 0 ^ % \| f F t T
```
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.custom_motions

options.description: To remap any key to normal! commands.
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.custom_noremaps

options.description: To remap VM mappings to other VM mappings.
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.custom_remaps

options.description:
Default mappings are `permanent`, that is, always available, and applied when Vim starts.

Buffer mappings instead are applied per-buffer, when VM is started.
Permanent mappings, except `<C-n>`, can be disabled by setting this option to `0`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.default_mappings

options.description:
Whether to disable syntax highlighting in insert mode.

You could want to do it for performance reasons.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.disable_syntax_in_imode

options.description: VM won't start if buffer size is greater than this.
options.type: null or unsigned integer, meaning >=0, or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.filesize_limit

options.description:
Controls VM default highlighting style for patterns matched, but not selected.

Possible useful values are `"underline"` and `"red"`.
Otherwise an empty string if you want the normal `|Search|` highlight, or a full highlight
command (help `|:hi|`).
options.type: null or string or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.highlight_matches

options.description:
Some keys in insert mode can have a different behaviour, compared to vim
defaults. Possible values:

- `"c-a"`: `<C-A>` go to the beginning of the line, at indent level
- `"c-e"`: `<C-E>` go to the end of the line
- `"c-v"`: `<C-V>` paste from VM unnamed register
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.insert_special_keys

options.description:
Mappings preceded by `\\` are meant prefixed with `|g:VM_leader|`.

Some of the permanent/visual mappings use the `|g:VM_leader|` as well, and you could want to
use a different one for them.
In this case you can define the leader as an attrs.
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.leader

options.description: Controls how often text is updated in insert mode.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.live_editing

options.description: Customize key mappings.
options.type: null or (attribute set of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.maps

options.description: Whether to enable mouse mappings.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.mouse_mappings

options.description:
If true VM registers will be stored in the `|viminfo|`.
The `viminfo` option must include `!`, for this to work.

Also see `|:VMRegisters|`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.persistent_registers

options.description: Used for plugins compatibility, see `|vm-compatibility|`.
options.type: null or (attribute set of (anything or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.plugins_compatibilty

options.description:
So that you don't have to type `<Esc>` twice.

If you set this to `1`, maybe you can remap `Reselect Last`, so that you can quickly restart VM
with your last selection.
See `|vm-quick-reference|`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.quit_after_leaving_insert_mode

options.description:
When executing normal commands in cursor mode (`dw` and similar), by default recursive mappings
are used, so that user text object can be used as well.

Set to `0` if you always want commands in cursor mode to be non-recursive.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.recursive_operations_at_cursors

options.description:
Autoindentation (via `|indentkeys|`) is temporarily disabled in insert mode, and you have to
reindent edited lines yoursef.

For filetypes included in this list, edited lines are automatically reindented when exiting
insert mode.
options.type: null or (list of (string or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.reindent_filetypes

options.description: The first region will be reselected after most commands, if set to `1`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.reselect_first

options.description:
Enable statusline when VM is active.
- With a value of `1`, the statusline will be set once, on VM start.
- With a value of `2`, the statusline will be refreshed on `|CursorHold|` event.
- With a value of `3`, also on `|CursorMoved|` event.
options.type: null or one of 1, 2, 3 or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.set_statusline

options.description:
When entering VM and there are mapping conflicts, a warning is displayed.

Set to `0` to disable this warning.
You can still run `|:VMDebug|` to see if there are conflicts.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.show_warnings

options.description:
Don't display a message when exiting VM.

You may prefer it if you already set up statusline integration.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.silent_exit

options.description:
If insert mode is entered while `|vm-single-mode|` is enabled, it will be reset automatically
when exiting insert mode, unless this value is `0`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.single_mode_auto_reset

options.description:
Set to `0` to disable entirely insert mode mappings to cycle cursors in `|vm-single-mode|`.

If you only want to change the default mappings, see `|vm-mappings-buffer|`.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.single_mode_maps

options.description: When adding cursors up/down, skip empty lines.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.skip_empty_lines

options.description: When adding cursors up/down, skip shorter lines.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.skip_shorter_lines

options.description:
In insert mode, the active cursor is normally the last selected one.

Set this option to `1` to always use the first cursor in the line.
options.type: null or (one of 0, 1) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.use_first_cursor_in_line

options.description:
Cursor mode only.

The elements of the list can be simple strings (then any text object can be accepted) or an
attrs with the operator as key, and the number of characters to be typed as value.

These operators can be either vim or plugin operators, mappings are passed recursively.

Note: `|vim-surround|` and `|vim-abolish|` have built-in support, this isn't needed for them
to work.
options.type: null or (list of (string or attribute set of (unsigned integer, meaning >=0) or raw lua code)) or raw lua code
options.title: plugins.visual-multi.settings.user_operators

options.description:

possible.

Define the storage mode for ring values.

Using `shada`, this will save pesistantly using Neovim ShaDa feature.
This means that history will be persisted between each session of Neovim.

You can also use this feature to sync the yank history across multiple running instances
of Neovim by updating shada file.
If you execute `:wshada` in the first instance and then `:rshada` in the second instance,
the second instance will be synced with the yank history in the first instance.

options.description:
Yanky can automatically adds to ring history yanks that occurs outside of Neovim.
This works regardless to your `&clipboard` setting.

This means, if `&clipboard` is set to `unnamed` and/or `unnamedplus`, if you yank
something outside of Neovim, you can put it immediately using `p` and it will be added to
your yank ring.

If `&clipboard` is empty, if you yank something outside of Neovim, this will be the first
value you'll have when cycling through the ring.
Basically, you can do `p` and then `<c-p>` to paste yanked text.

Note that `clipboard == unnamed` uses the primary selection of the system (see
`:h clipboard` for more details) which is updated on selection, not on copy/yank.
Also note that the syncing happens when neovim gains focus.

options.description:
While opening an attachment, Zotcite cannot catch errors because it doesn't wait for the
application to finish.

If zotcite fails to open a PDF attachment, you may want to temporarily set this option to
`true`.

Then, Neovim should freeze until the attachment is closed, and, if the PDF viewer finishes
with non-zero status, anything output to the `stderr` will be displayed as a warning message.

options.description:
Preview handler for `'inccommand'`, see `:h command-preview`.

The function is called with `opts`, `ns`, and `buf` arguments. `opts` has the same form as
`nvim_create_user_command()` callbacks, `ns` is the preview highlight namespace, and `buf`
is the preview buffer for `inccommand=split` or `nil` for `inccommand=nosplit`.

Return `0` to show no preview, `1` to show a preview without opening the preview window, or
`2` to open the preview window when `inccommand=split`.
options.example:
''
  function(opts, ns, buf)
    if buf then
      vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf, 0, -1, false, { opts.args })
    end
    return 2
  end
''
